plan.planning_summary: This plan initiates the first of two allowed research rounds for a two-layer antireflection coating design. Since no literature evidence is available (evidence_ids_allowed is empty), the route is theory-based, relying on fundamental thin-film interference principles. The strategy splits the discrete 'layer order' decision into two separate, parallel-executable routes to ensure the global minimum is not missed due to local optimizer trapping in one topology. Route 01 tests the [Air | SiO2 | TiO2 | Glass] configuration, while Route 02 tests [Air | TiO2 | SiO2 | Glass]. Both routes optimize continuous thickness variables within the 40-160 nm bounds using a deterministic grid search followed by local refinement, constrained to 64 evaluations total per route as per the problem statement.

routes.title: Optimization of SiO2-over-TiO2 Two-Layer AR Stack
routes.scientific_hypothesis: For a two-layer system with indices n_air=1.0, n_SiO2=1.46, n_TiO2=2.40, n_glass=1.52, placing the lower-index SiO2 layer adjacent to air and the higher-index TiO2 layer adjacent to the substrate will yield a broader spectral minimum or a lower mean reflectance in the 450-700 nm band compared to the reverse order, provided optimal thicknesses are found within the 40-160 nm constraints.
routes.design_principle: Impedance matching via stepped refractive index profile (1.0 -> 1.46 -> 2.40 -> 1.52) to minimize Fresnel reflections through destructive interference across the visible band.
routes.proposed_topology: exactly 6 alternating SiO2 (n=1.46)/TiO2 (n=2.40) pairs (12 finite layers)
soft_objectives: Minimize arithmetic mean power reflectance (s-pol, normal incidence) over 450-700 nm
manufacturing_considerations: Thickness bounds strictly enforced between 40 nm and 160 nm
theory_basis: Transfer Matrix Method for multilayer interference
Quarter-wave and modified quarter-wave antireflection conditions
expected_advantages: Smoother index transition from air to substrate may reduce sensitivity to wavelength variations
Standard high-low index pairing often yields robust broadband performance
known_risks: The specific thickness constraints (40-160 nm) may prevent reaching the theoretical quarter-wave optimum for both layers simultaneously
Local minima in the optimization landscape may trap the solver if the initial grid is too coarse
routes.execution_request_english: Execute a deterministic optimization for a planar stack: Air | SiO2 (n=1.46) | TiO2 (n=2.40) | Glass (n=1.52). Variables: thickness of SiO2 and TiO2, both bounded [40, 160] nm. Objective: Minimize arithmetic mean s-polarized power reflectance at 0 degrees incidence over wavelengths 450, 455, ..., 700 nm. Method: Perform a coarse grid search (8x8 points) followed by Nelder-Mead simplex refinement, totaling max 64 function evaluations. Seed: 17. Output the optimal thickness pair, the full reflectance spectrum, and the calculated mean reflectance. Topology realization override: disregard any symbolic repeat count, range, or ellipsis above and use exactly 6 alternating SiO2 (n=1.46)/TiO2 (n=2.40) pairs (12 finite layers). Optimize only continuous physical thicknesses; the task compiler must fully expand every finite layer. Canonical user controls: incidence angles 0 degrees. polarization s. wavelength intervals 450-700 nm. soft objectives: minimized arithmetic mean power reflectance in the 450-700 nm band; mean reflectance below 0.03 as a soft scoring preference. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high reflection in the 450-700 nm band. manufacturing constraints: layer thickness bounds: 40 nm to 160 nm; exactly one layer of SiO2 and one layer of TiO2.

routes.title: Optimization of TiO2-over-SiO2 Two-Layer AR Stack
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Placing the higher-index TiO2 layer adjacent to air and the lower-index SiO2 layer adjacent to the glass substrate (1.0 -> 2.40 -> 1.46 -> 1.52) may yield a superior global minimum for mean reflectance in the 450-700 nm band compared to the reverse order, specifically by leveraging the strong phase shift at the air-TiO2 interface to cancel reflections more effectively within the limited thickness budget.
routes.design_principle: Inverse impedance stepping where the high-index layer acts as a primary reflector cancellator at the air interface, tuned by the second low-index layer.
routes.proposed_topology: exactly 6 alternating TiO2 (n=2.40)/SiO2 (n=1.46) pairs (12 finite layers)
soft_objectives: Minimize arithmetic mean power reflectance (s-pol, normal incidence) over 450-700 nm
manufacturing_considerations: Thickness bounds strictly enforced between 40 nm and 160 nm
theory_basis: Transfer Matrix Method for multilayer interference
Phase compensation effects in high-index first layers
expected_advantages: High index contrast at the first interface allows for thinner physical layers to achieve required optical path differences
May provide better performance if the ideal quarter-wave thickness for the low-index material exceeds the 160 nm limit
known_risks: Large index jump at air interface might create narrowband rather than broadband cancellation
Risk of higher average reflectance if the second layer cannot adequately compensate the residual reflection

research_influence: Absence of literature evidence (evidence_ids_allowed is empty) necessitated a purely theory-based approach relying on fundamental TMM physics and comparative topology testing.
The strict limit of 64 evaluations per round dictated the use of a hybrid coarse-grid-plus-local-search strategy rather than a global stochastic optimizer.
unresolved_decisions: Which layer ordering (SiO2/TiO2 vs TiO2/SiO2) provides the global minimum reflectance under the specific 40-160 nm thickness constraints.
Whether the soft target of mean reflectance < 0.03 is physically achievable with only two layers of these specific materials.
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: Stop after the bounded route portfolio is exhausted or further search stagnates. Return every physically verified candidate and report soft objective trade-offs without a performance admission threshold.
